body.x: Rehabilitation progress is usually measured in a clinic, with a therapist and a goniometer, a visit at a time. Between those visits, how the exercises actually go is mostly invisible.
The Hong Kong Polytechnic University was named a 2027 Honoree in Digital Health at the CES 2027 Innovation Awards for the Smart Motion Capture App for Rehabilitation (SMCAR).

SMCAR turns a standard iPhone or iPad running iOS 17 or later into a clinical-grade, markerless motion-capture system for remote rehabilitation. The description says it uses ARKit and a hybrid CNN-Transformer pose-estimation algorithm to track 22 body joints with under 15 degrees mean absolute error, and gives dual real-time feedback: a virtual avatar mirroring the patient's motion and live graphs of joint-angle changes.

A hybrid guidance system overlays the user's augmented-reality skeleton alongside an instructor video, adjusting playback speed to performance gaps. It automates active range of motion (AROM) measurements without clinician-administered goniometer tests, stores longitudinal performance data and supports standardized motor-impairment assessments such as the Fugl-Meyer.

By delivering laboratory-grade kinematic analysis on consumer devices with under 10ms rendering latency, the description says SMCAR widens access to precision neurorehabilitation, enabling continuous remote monitoring and adaptive exercise progression.

The CES Innovation Awards program, an annual competition honoring outstanding design and engineering in consumer technology products, recognizes all recipients as Honorees at two levels. The Honoree level covers products that score above the scoring threshold in each category, while Best of Innovation goes to the highest-scoring Honorees. A panel of industry expert judges and global media scores each product on engineering and functionality, aesthetic and design, and what makes it unique and innovative.

body.x: AVING NEWS, a global media company with 21 years of experience covering CES, operates AVING CES Newsroom (avingces.news), a dedicated platform for delivering the latest innovations to global audiences. Publishing more than 1,000 articles and conducting hundreds of on-site video interviews annually, AVING NEWS has helped Korean startups gain international visibility and expand their global reach. At CES 2027, AVING NEWS will operate the AVING TECH TALK broadcast zone at the Venetian Expo (Hall A, Booth 50271), providing on-site coverage and interviews that spotlight Korean companies and their latest innovations.

Ahead of CES 2027, AVING NEWS will host the 3rd Innovation Awards Winners Networking Party at MIK BASE CAMP on Wednesday, November 25, at 5 p.m. The event will also feature individual video interviews with participating companies, with registration available through Eventus. In early December, AVING NEWS will begin its pre-show coverage, including an interview program connecting Korean innovators with U.S. media outlets that regularly cover CES and participate in the Innovation Awards judging process.
